notes: Second full audit, covering everything since feeb9a8 (rounds 2-5) and the first push to GitHub. Static Next.js export: no backend, no auth, no forms, no database, no payments, no AI calls, no analytics. Checked: (1) secrets: none in the working tree or in git history (no .env, key, certificate or credential file was ever committed); .gitignore hardened before the push to cover keys/certificates (*.pem *.key *.crt *.p12 *.pfx *.jks), credential files (.npmrc .netrc *credentials* service-account*.json), host tooling (.vercel .wrangler .netlify .aws .terraform, *.tfstate) and editor/OS noise; no tracked file is caught by the new rules. (2) injection: the only dangerouslySetInnerHTML is components/seo/JsonLd.tsx, which escapes < before serialising; no eval, no new Function, no innerHTML; the six client components (lyrics dialog, lightbox, copy-email, two embed facades, language switcher) render server-passed children and never build markup from strings. (3) content validation: every URL in content/ now goes through httpUrl (zod, protocol pinned to http/https); SiteSchema.url was the one field still on bare z.url(), which in zod 4 accepts javascript: and data:, and is now pinned as well; gallery keys are constrained to /^[a-z0-9-]+$/ and checked against the image manifest at build. (4) deployment: public/_headers keeps CSP (script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', unavoidable for a static export that inlines RSC payloads; no unsafe-eval; frame-src limited to youtube-nocookie.com and bandcamp.com; object-src none; base-uri self; form-action self; frame-ancestors none), HSTS preload, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP; the stale 'no eval needed for three.js' note was corrected since three.js is gone; the production build emits no browser source maps and only out/ is deployed. (5) CI: both workflows now declare least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN scopes (contents: read for CI, permissions: {} for the weekly rebuild); the Cloudflare deploy hook is read from a repository secret into an env var and never echoed. (6) third parties: YouTube and Bandcamp load only after a click, nothing is stored, external links carry rel=noopener. (7) dependencies: npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities in production dependencies; 7 advisories remain in dev-only tooling (extract-zip, qs, tmp, uuid, via the lighthouse and serve chains), none reachable at runtime and none fixable without a breaking change. Findings: no Critical, no High. Medium: SiteSchema.url accepted any URL scheme (fixed). Low: unconstrained gallery image keys (fixed), unscoped workflow token permissions (fixed), CSP relies on 'unsafe-inline' for scripts (documented, inherent to static export), the booking address is published in plain text in the Impressum (required by German law, accepted), dev-dependency advisories to revisit at the next tooling update.
